description: AirForestry's electric drones thin forests from the air without damaging the ground or the surrounding trees. Through thinning, the company reduces carbon dioxide emissions from forestry work while increasing the forest's ability to sequester carbon by freeing up 20% of forest land that is currently used for forestry access roads.
Instead of using refrigerant gases with high global warming potential, Barocal’s technology uses new solid-state, temperature-changing materials that are cheap and non-toxic.

Bramble Energy is powering the transition to net zero with unique fuel cell technology. Using bonded layers of printed circuit boards, rather than metal plates and manifolds, they’ve created a low cost, lightweight, digital alternative that can be manufactured in almost any PCB factory across the globe.

C-Capture is creating new possibilities for the net zero transition. Their unique, solvent-based technology offers a safe and low-cost way to remove carbon dioxide from energy and industrial processes, based on a new class of carbon capture chemistry invented at the University of Leeds.

First Light’s unique target designs are the key technology. They have two aspects, the amplifier and the fuel capsule. The amplifier boosts the pressure of projectile impact and creates convergence, focusing shockwaves onto the fuel capsule.

Hysata is set to play a central role in the trillion-dollar hydrogen economy with its new ultra-high efficiency electrolyser. Their scientific breakthrough in alkaline electrolysis uses capillary action to transport water into the cell, via the membrane, giving an overall system efficiency of up to 95% HHV. With a highly scalable manufacturing process, Hysata has the potential to make green hydrogen competitive years earlier than previously assumed, accelerating the transition to net zero.

Magnomatics is changing gears to tackle some of the largest challenges for net zero. By replacing teeth with magnets, gears become more efficient, adaptable and durable. The upshot? The potential to improve everything from renewable energy to railways.

Mantle8's proprietary technology combines geology, geophysics, and geochemistry data to create highly accurate predictive models for natural hydrogen detection. Multiphysics imaging technology can visualize the entire hydrogen generating system to evaluate the amount and quality of hydrogen present. This proprietary technology is scalable for the assessment and exploration of the entire planet

Mixergy applies thermodynamics from Oxford to one of the biggest challenges in climate change: heat in buildings. Coupling and coordinating electrical heating systems, like immersion heaters and heat pumps, with electricity supply from the grid or solar panels, Mixergy dramatically increases efficiency and reduces costs, bringing forward the advent of carbon-free heat.
Delivering a step change in energy density by creating class-leading battery materials to realise a more sustainable world.

Oxa is leading the charge towards sustainable mobility for all, improving safety and enhancing access with ground breaking autonomous vehicle technology at scale. Spun out of the world-leading Oxford Robotics Institute, its adaptable universal platform delivers infrastructure-free autonomy for any vehicle type in any environment.

University of Oxford spin-out focused on turning CO2 directly into jet fuel range hydrocarbons using a novel, one-step catalyst and process. Their vision is to give future generations the acknowledged benefits of hydrocarbons but without their climate impact.
tado° is the European leader in intelligent home climate management. Its smart thermostats curb heating costs by 22% on average. Its smart time-of-use tariffs allow for next-generation energy pricing
Vytal is the largest digital re-use system for food packaging in take-away and delivery. Deposit free and used by 1,000s of partners in 8 countries.
